sentences.text: This matter is taken up by video conferencing mode.

2. The Petitioner apprehending his arrest in Badambadi P.S. Case No.142 of 2021 registered for alleged commission of offences punishable under Sections 417, 420, 272 and 273 of the I.P.C. read with Sections 51, 52, 57, 59, 63 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and Section 20 of the Cigarettes and other Tobacco Products Act, 2003, has filed this petition for his release on pre-arrest bail.

entities.text: Cigarettes and other Tobacco Products Act, 2003
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
3. Heard the learned counsel for the Petitioner and the learned counsel for the State.
4. Regard being had to the facts and submissions made, especially the nature and gravity of accusation, circumstances in which the offence alleged to have been committed and also there being nothing on record to show that the allegation has // 2 // been made against the Petitioner being actuated with mala fide, this Court is not inclined to release the Petitioner on pre-arrest bail.
5. Accordingly, the prayer for pre-arrest bail of the Petitioner stands rejected and the ABLAPL is disposed of being dismissed.

6. As the restrictions due to resurgence of COVID-19 situation are continuing, learned counsel for the parties may utilize a printout of the order available in the High Court's website, at par with certified copy, subject to attestation by the concerned advocate, in the manner prescribed vide Court's Notice No.4587, dated 25th March, 2020 as modified by Court's Notice No.4798, dated 15th Bijoy Kumar Kamani vs State Of Odisha ....
